answer.decision: Choose jittered expirations, request coalescing, and stale-while-revalidate.
answer.action: Today, enable per-key single-flight for the endpoint and serve cached values during refresh for up to 90 seconds, with refresh timeouts and leader-failure recovery. Add bounded TTL jitter so hot keys expire at different times. Enforce a hard maximum served-object age of five minutes across the fresh and stale windows. Roll out gradually while monitoring cache hit rate, origin QPS and CPU, coalesced requests, stale serves, refresh latency and failures; then load-test the observed 120-hot-key traffic pattern.
reasons: Repeated work on only 120 keys caused 91 percent of the origin CPU spike, making request coalescing the most direct immediate mitigation.
The existing cache client already supports single-flight, allowing origin load to be reduced today without replacing the cache product.
Jitter addresses synchronized expiration, while stale-while-revalidate prevents requests from blocking on or duplicating refresh work.
The incident's cache-hit-rate collapse indicates that expiration bursts materially shifted traffic to the origin.
A global TTL increase could violate the five-minute freshness requirement, while database scaling did not prevent saturation under duplicate load.
assumptions: Single-flight can be enabled per key for this endpoint without a cache-product replacement.
The cache layer tracks object age accurately enough to enforce the five-minute hard limit.
TTL jitter, refresh timing, and the stale-serving window are configurable so their combined behavior cannot serve data older than five minutes.
risks: Incorrect age calculations or window configuration could breach the freshness requirement.
A failed or stalled single-flight leader could delay refreshes without strict timeouts, cleanup, and retry behavior.
Refresh failures near the five-minute limit may require rejecting requests or querying the origin rather than continuing to serve stale data.
A gradual rollout still requires careful monitoring because coalescing may shift latency or failure behavior to leader requests.

citations.claim: Cache hit rate fell from 94 percent to 37 percent within 40 seconds during the incident.
Repeated queries for the same 120 keys accounted for 91 percent of the origin CPU spike.
The cache client already exposes a disabled single-flight primitive.
Endpoint data must remain no more than five minutes stale.
Database scaling reduced query latency but did not prevent saturation under repeated duplicate requests.
Serving stale cached values for up to 90 seconds during refresh is acceptable if the five-minute freshness bound is preserved.
